newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Gorbachev launches Vienna nuclear safety body.
newsitem.headline: Gorbachev launches Vienna nuclear safety body.

text.p: Former Soviet president Mikhail Gorbachev on Thursday launched an independent nuclear safety organisation, aimed at stepping up pressure on governments to improve nuclear safety standards by mobilising public opinion.
Gorbachev told a news conference at the launch that he had agreed to be president of the International Nuclear Safety Foundation (INSF), which will be based in Vienna.
"We are not satisfied. There are pockets of nuclear insecurity everywhere and we want to highlight the problems for the public," he told reporters.
He cited the example of reactors of disused nuclear submarines in northern Russia as an enormous potential danger that needed to be addressed.
However, the author of groundbreaking glasnost and perestroika policies in the former Soviet Union was unable to provide any exact details on immediate plans of the organisation.
He said a board of experienced trustees had been formed which would first define their specific goals and then use their contacts to try to raise funds from the international business community.
They had also enroled the support of scientists and economists worldwide who would be able to advise the group.
"A lot has already been done but a lot more must be done," he said. "We want to prevent another Chernobyl or even a smaller accident of that kind."

The INSF plans to cooperate with existing organisations and assist them with its additional expertise. The U.N. nuclear body, the International Atomic Energy Agency, and the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty Organisation are both based in Vienna.
But Gorbachev stressed that the new group did not want to get involved in international nuclear weapons treaties.

"We have never wanted to do the job of the U.S., French, German or Russian governments. It's their responsibility to their citizens and world community according to the agreements signed which concern nuclear weapons and the disposal of nuclear waste," he said.
